k:multilingual-eval-instructions@1.2:db7.excerpt:
## Content-quality rubric
These grades concern task-quality defects. Language QA must establish context and impact for disputed locale-specific cases.

| Dimension | Major defect | Minor defect | Acceptable / no automatic penalty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Language adherence | Substantial unrequested language mismatch violating the requirement | Limited genuine mismatch with a stated requirement | Ordinary loanwords or switching permitted by the task |
| Register / honorifics | Unmotivated, materially disruptive inconsistency confirmed in context | Localized inappropriate shift with limited effect | Natural variation, quotation or a justified addressee change |
| Regional appropriateness | Clear material mismatch with the specified audience | Localized genuine mismatch with limited effect | Regional vocabulary natural for the intended audience |
| Naturalness | Demonstrable phrasing problems that materially impair meaning or appropriate use | Identifiable localized awkwardness | A reviewer preference without an identifiable error |

k:multilingual-eval-instructions@1.2:b26.excerpt:
## Regional variation and naturalness
Assess wording against the specified locale or audience. Natural Southern Vietnamese vocabulary is not an error merely because a Northern reviewer prefers a different word. Reviewer preference or a majority vote alone does not establish a linguistic defect; identify the wording and its effect.

k:multilingual-eval-faq@1.1:c080929d.excerpt:
## Register and honorifics

### Q: Who scores Korean or Japanese register shifts?
Route the case to appropriate Korean or Japanese language QA with exact sentence endings and surrounding context. Check quotations and addressee changes. The task-quality grade depends on demonstrated impact; do not assign a major penalty from the presence of a shift alone.

### Q: Spanish tú versus usted inconsistency — major or minor?
Ask Spanish QA to check addressee, intended formality and discourse context. An unjustified shift can be an error, but its grade needs a case-specific rationale.

[PRIOR RECORD (advice_review; decision_status: tl_approved; execution_status: not_executed; outcome_status: not_observed) - history, not a standing rule.]
# Approve English field names for the audit index

## Evidence available at review

The September 28 audit packet used mixed headings for the same metadata field: task_id, ID de tarea, and タスクID. The review coordinator manually matched three equivalent columns. The packet also included original Spanish and Japanese text excerpts; no defect in those excerpts was alleged.

The proposed index convention uses English metadata keys task_id, locale, and reviewer_id, with attachment names multi11_<locale>_<task_id>.txt. Only the administrative labels and filenames would change. No index revision has been published yet.

## Prior ThreadSense advice

Use English throughout audit packets so cross-language reviewers can navigate them consistently.

## TL response

Approve a narrower documentation edit: English keys and predictable filenames for the internal audit index. Preserve original-language prompts, responses, and quoted evidence. Do not translate the evaluated content or treat an English index field as evidence that a model switched languages.

k:multilingual-eval-faq@1.1:9ea83675.excerpt:
## Regional variation

### Q: Are Vietnamese regional words always penalized?
No. Confirm the intended locale or audience. Vocabulary natural for that audience is acceptable even when another reviewer would use a different regional term. If the required locale is unclear, obtain that context before deciding.
